look_here_first: Turn an INTACT MATURE CAPSULE sideways. At the transverse lid/seam find a distinct thin papery circular WING roughly 0.5–1.5 mm wide, BELOW the opening line, wrapping completely around the green fruit. Verify on multiple mature capsules; with broad flat leaves this is stronger than flower color. Oleracea has a lid without expanded wing; pilosa has narrow leaf blades, prominent white hair tufts and an unwinged fruit. Cultivated 'Wildfire' images are reference only, not a wild Texas taxonomic voucher.

morphology_keys.habit: Annual, fleshy branching prostrate to ascending herb with fibrous roots and mostly smooth stems, sparse node hairs.
morphology_keys.leaves: Simple flat succulent leaves, obovate/spatulate or lanceolate, 10–35 × 2–15 mm, apex rounded, truncate or slightly pointed; 4–5 upper subtending leaves near flowers.
morphology_keys.flowers: Usually 8–15 mm diam; typically yellow, or yellow tipped red/copper in certain named taxa and cultivated forms, 7–30 stamens. Color cannot prove wild subspecies.
morphology_keys.fruits: Ovoid/turbinate capsule 3–5 mm diameter with horizontally opening lid and EXPANDED papery wing 0.5–1.5 mm wide beneath suture (unique in local lesson).
morphology_keys.seeds: Gray flattened 0.5–1 mm, stellate cell pattern with longer tubercles; measured macro needed.
morphology_keys.axils: Sparse/inconspicuous white trichomes at nodes and near inflorescences; not large white clumps like pilosa.
best_field_traits: Mature capsule with full circumference papery wing 0.5–1.5 mm proximal to the lid seam: strongest cue.
Flat succulent leaves may overlap common purslane; never identify on leaves alone.
Axillary hairs sparse compared with shaggy purslane.
Photo of nursery cultivar 'Wildfire' shows species-level wing anatomy but does NOT validate a wild Texas subspecies.
Native at Texas state level per Kew, but 3-target-county validation remains UNRESOLVED.

confused_with: Cultivated Portulaca umbraticola hybrids or cultivars
comparisons.key_distinctions: Winged mature fruit seam versus unwinged oleracea and pilosa. Pilosa narrow leaves and woolly axils; oleracea flat broad leaves but no encircling wing. Nursery 'Wildfire Mixed' may originate in South American material; species morphology photo cannot document local wild subspecies or locality.
